rules: RTL-first layouts; Latin terms are isolated LTR islands (.term)
no uppercase concept — overlines are sentence case
Ghorab has no Latin glyphs: an English term inside a Ghorab headline falls to Montserrat 700 at ×0.925

colour._annotationRule: Must differ from the primary and from any action colour, so an annotation can never be mistaken for interface.

arabicDisplay.note: licence-restricted; a labelled placeholder stands in where team hosting is not clearly permitted

sketch._note: Latin-only. A handwritten note in Arabic silently falls back and stops being handwriting — use digits or an established Latin term instead.

impactHook._constraint: NOT a universal rule. With the CURRENT Impact Hook style only — Montserrat Black, 140 px, line height 128, tracking -3%, Latin uppercase — a hook column narrower than about 740 px cannot hold words longer than about five characters without breaking mid-word. It is a property of this style at this size in this column, and it changes the moment any of those change. Treat it as a setting to check, not a law: widen the column, shorten the word, or adjust the style.

watermark._variantRule: Every other themeable component in the system takes Light/Dark from the Color / Semantic mode. The watermark cannot: it responds to the luminance of the MEDIA underneath the corner, which the semantic mode does not know. A dark photograph on a light slide takes Glass Dark. So the glass tone is a variant, and its mark fill binds to a primitive rather than a mark/* semantic, on purpose.
watermark.inset: x = canvas margin, y = canvas reserve-top — read from the canvas or video profile, never hard-coded. Where a canvas has no top reserve (thumbnails) y falls back to the margin.

composition.subjectScale: The dominant subject occupies 40-70% of the canvas and bleeds off at least one edge. A subject small enough to sit inside a margin has already failed.
composition.textPanels: forbidden — contrast comes from a global grade over the image

archetypes._note: CANDIDATE INSTANCES of composition strategies, never a lookup from content type to layout.

mediaRequirements._note: What each archetype needs from the shoot. Adopted from the Canva reference review, where the one substantive build guide in the account declared photo slots per direction and said plainly "if the shoot is thin, use A". Choosing an archetype you do not have the imagery for is the most expensive mistake available.
mediaRequirements.01 PRODUCT DOMINANT: 1 frame — the product lit and isolated enough to bleed off one edge.
mediaRequirements.02 FACE + PRODUCT: 2 frames — a close reaction and a product shot; or 1 frame holding both with room to crop.
mediaRequirements.03 A/B COMPARISON: 2 frames at MATCHED scale, angle and lighting. Mismatched framing makes the comparison dishonest before a word is read.
mediaRequirements.04 SCREEN / FEATURE EMPHASIS: 1 screenshot or macro frame, sharp on the feature, calm around it.
mediaRequirements.05 SKETCH / ANNOTATION: 1 frame with an identifiable focal point to mark and calm space beside it for the hook.
mediaRequirements.06 BIG CLAIM: 1 frame, or none — the claim can carry the frame on an expressive ground alone.
mediaRequirements.07 VISUAL CONTRADICTION: 2 frames (the claim and its counter-example), or 1 frame plus a struck hook.
mediaRequirements.08 PROBLEM / FIX: 2 frames of the same subject in two states, same framing.
mediaRequirements.09 TRANSFORMATION: 2 frames, or 1 frame recomposed two ways.
mediaRequirements.10 MINIMAL PREMIUM: 1 frame strong enough to carry a quiet composition. On an ordinary photo this archetype fails.
mediaRequirements.thin-shoot: With a single usable frame use 01, 05 or 06. Never force a two-frame archetype by duplicating one photograph — a comparison between a picture and itself is a lie.

checklist: One dominant subject at 40-70% of the canvas, bleeding off at least one edge.
Hook is 2-5 words and is NOT the video title.
Every annotation points at something real, or there is no annotation.
No panel behind the text — contrast is a global grade over the whole image.
Watermark present exactly once, in a free safe corner.
On any surface with a 1:1 preview, everything that must survive sits inside tile/centre-safe.
Established Latin terms left in Latin; Arabic never letter-spaced; Western digits.
No gradient, no emoji, no arrow used as decoration.
Exported from the platform profile that matches the destination.
